title: 2019 AMC 12B Problem 9
statement: For how many integral values of \(x\) can a triangle of positive area be formed having side lengths \(\log_2 x,\) \(\log_4 x,\) and \(3?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(t=\log_2 x.\) Then \(\log_4 x=\dfrac{t}{2},\) and the sides are \(t,\ \dfrac{t}{2},\ 3.\)

The triangle inequalities give \(t+\dfrac{t}{2}\gt3\) (so \(t\gt2\)) and \(\dfrac{t}{2}+3\gt t\) (so \(t\lt6\)); the third inequality is automatic.

Thus \(2\lt\log_2 x\lt6,\) i.e. \(4\lt x\lt64.\) The integers \(5,6,\ldots,63\) number \(59.\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Apply the triangle inequality to sides \(t,\ \dfrac{t}{2},\ 3\)
